project.title: Arkaik (Self Map)

maps.title: Studio journey

maps.title: Platform wiring

maps.title: Data spine

maps.title: Promise coverage

nodes.title: /projects
nodes.description: The projects home: Hosted / Synked / Lokal sections with per-section create menus, project cards, the Explore public self-map, empty states, and the generated-JSON import prompt.

nodes.title: Projects Actions Routing
nodes.description: Routes every way into a project from the /projects home — create, import JSON, load an example, or move a browser project into the account — with the signed-in state deciding which sections and targets are on offer.

cases.label: Create in a section (Hosted / Synked / Lokal)
Move a browser project into the account

nodes.title: Import Project JSON
nodes.description: Bring a project bundle in from a JSON file on the projects page — parsed, schema-migrated, validated with readable path-level errors, and landed locally under a collision-free id that can never squat the hosted or seed namespaces.

entries.label: Bundle passes parse, migration, and validation?

nodes.title: Create Project
nodes.description: Create a new empty project in a chosen section: Hosted goes straight to the account, Synked saves locally then backs up immediately, Lokal stays in this browser.

nodes.title: Delete Project
nodes.description: Delete a project from its Settings danger zone — confirm by typing the title, then land back on the projects home.

nodes.title: Import Example Projects
nodes.description: Load a bundled example (Pebbles or Arkaik's own self-map) into this browser as a Lokal project, offered where the Lokal section or the signed-out page is empty.

nodes.title: ProjectBundle
nodes.description: The canonical, schema-versioned interchange document defined in @arkaik/schema: one project plus its nodes, edges, and an optional embedded journal, parsed and validated on every import and write.

nodes.title: Two axes: status is delivery, stage is exposure
nodes.description: Node status stays a pure delivery lifecycle; exposure concerns live on the separate stage axis instead of being folded into status.

metadata.context: Early proposals for the status overhaul considered adding `limited` and `deprecated` as statuses in their own right, but that would have conflated exposure — how visible or available a node is — with delivery lifecycle, where a node sits in the build pipeline.
metadata.consequences: The stage axis keeps expressing exposure on its own terms; the status list stays a clean seven-value delivery lifecycle with no exposure concepts mixed in; `limited` and `deprecated` were rejected as statuses and never entered the vocabulary.

nodes.title: Blocked is a flag, not a status
nodes.description: A blocked node keeps its lifecycle status; blockage is recorded as a metadata flag instead of a status value.

metadata.context: A blocked node parked in a dedicated `blocked` status lost its lifecycle position the moment it got blocked — there was no way to tell whether it had been in backlog or in development.
metadata.consequences: `metadata.blocked_by` now carries the dependency reference directly; a blocked node keeps its underlying status untouched; the node library filters on the flag rather than on a separate status value.

nodes.title: Status migrations: hard cutover + permanent aliases
nodes.description: The v2-to-v3 status vocabulary remap runs once, at import, with the retired ids accepted forever afterward as parse-time aliases.

metadata.context: Soft-deprecating the old ids (`prioritized`, `blocked`, and the pre-v3 meaning of `backlog`) would have left every consumer — the app, the CLI, the MCP server — carrying dual-vocabulary branches forever.
metadata.consequences: A one-time, version-gated remap runs on any bundle below schema_version 3 and stamps the new version; the retired ids `prioritized` and `blocked` are accepted as permanent parse-time aliases from then on; journal history is never rewritten, so historical events keep their original vocabulary.

nodes.title: Project
nodes.description: The root identity of a bundle: id, title, optional version label, root_node_id, and metadata carrying maps, map display overrides, and product definitions.

nodes.title: Node
nodes.description: The atomic graph unit: one of six species (flow, view, data-model, api-endpoint, acceptance, decision) with a title, lifecycle status, platforms, and species-specific metadata.

nodes.title: Edge
nodes.description: A typed directed relationship between two nodes — composes, calls, displays, queries, covers, supersedes, generates, or impacts — validated against per-type source/target rules.

nodes.title: JournalEvent
nodes.description: A ULID-identified, append-only history event (node.created, node.status_changed, release.tagged, deliverable.shipped, ...) with timestamp and actor; history only ever grows.

nodes.title: MapDefinition
nodes.description: A saved map stored in project.metadata.maps: kind (journey or system), species and edge-type filters, root anchor, product scope, layout hints, and card display options.

nodes.title: Product
nodes.description: A ProductDefinition in project.metadata.products that scopes flows, views, and acceptances into one product; membership for other species is derived by traversal.

nodes.title: Deliverable
nodes.description: A projection computed from deliverable.shipped journal events: one unit of shipped work (typically a merged PR) with a summary, URL, and touched node ids, sitting between events and releases.

nodes.title: projects
nodes.description: IndexedDB (Dexie) store with one row per local project, keyed by project id, holding the journal-less BundleSnapshot so a mutation rewrites only that project's row.

nodes.title: journals
nodes.description: IndexedDB (Dexie) store with one row per project holding its embedded journal events; appends grow this row without ever re-serializing the graph snapshot.

nodes.title: meta
nodes.description: Small IndexedDB key/value store for local-provider bookkeeping — currently just the one-time legacy localStorage migration flag.

nodes.title: publik_snapshots
nodes.description: Postgres table of immutable anonymous shares: the journal-stripped, schema-validated bundle as jsonb plus an owner-key hash, size, and report count; re-publishing creates a new id.

nodes.title: publik_rate_limits
nodes.description: Postgres table of append-only throttle rows keyed by HMAC-hashed IP and action, counted over a sliding 1-hour window and pruned opportunistically — rate limiting with no Redis.

nodes.title: users
nodes.description: Auth.js adapter table of signed-in users, extended by arkaik with a tier column that selects the row in the TIER_LIMITS enforcement table.

nodes.title: accounts
nodes.description: Auth.js adapter table linking OAuth provider identities (GitHub at launch) to users, holding the provider's token response per linked account.

nodes.title: sessions
nodes.description: Auth.js adapter table for database sessions; unused on the request path because the session strategy is JWT, but created for adapter-schema completeness.

nodes.title: verification_token
nodes.description: Auth.js adapter table for email magic-link verification tokens; the email provider is deferred, so the table exists for adapter-contract completeness.

nodes.title: synk_projects
nodes.description: Postgres table with one row per backed-up local project, keyed by the composite (user_id, client project id) so two users can back up projects that share an id.

nodes.title: synk_backups
nodes.description: Postgres table of retained backup versions: the full bundle with journal as jsonb plus a server-computed sha256 for content-hash dedupe, pruned by retention per tier.

nodes.title: owners
nodes.description: Postgres table for the tenancy seam every hosted resource hangs off: today one derived personal owner per user (own-u<id>), forward-compatible with org owners.

nodes.title: owner_members
nodes.description: Postgres membership table joining users to owners with a role; getCaller resolves a caller's owner ids through it on every authenticated request.

nodes.title: api_tokens
nodes.description: Postgres table of machine credentials (ark_<prefix>_<secret>): a clear unique prefix for one-read lookup, a sha256 hash of the secret, scoped permissions, and revocation/expiry timestamps.

nodes.title: graph_projects
nodes.description: Postgres table of hosted product graphs: an owner-scoped jsonb snapshot (project + nodes + edges, no journal) with an optimistic-concurrency version bumped on every accepted mutation.

nodes.title: graph_events
nodes.description: Postgres append-only journal for hosted projects, keyed (project_id, event ULID) with a bigserial seq as the authoritative ordering — the server twin of the IndexedDB journals store.

nodes.title: project_repos
nodes.description: Postgres table linking hosted projects to the GitHub repositories that implement them, with an optional platform and a path_prefix so one monorepo can scope different subtrees to different platforms.

nodes.title: github_deliveries
nodes.description: Postgres webhook-delivery ledger: claiming a delivery id before applying it makes GitHub retries and manual redelivers idempotent, and rows older than a day are pruned on write.

nodes.title: GET/POST /api/auth/*
nodes.description: Auth.js catch-all route handling sign-in, the GitHub OAuth callback, and session reads; its adapter writes users and linked accounts on sign-in.

nodes.title: GET /api/auth/status
nodes.description: Client-facing auth status: returns whether auth is configured plus the signed-in user's public profile from the JWT session, never touching the database.

nodes.title: POST /api/github/webhook
nodes.description: The one endpoint accepting signed third-party requests: verifies the GitHub App HMAC over raw bytes, claims the delivery id for replay protection, then applies pull-request transitions to linked hosted projects.

nodes.title: GitHub API
nodes.description: Third-party surface arkaik calls back into: the OAuth token exchange during sign-in, and the App-authenticated pulls/{number}/files read that path-scoped monorepo links need.

nodes.title: GET/POST /api/graph/projects
nodes.description: Lists the caller's hosted graph projects and creates new ones from a validated bundle, enforcing the tier's project cap and seeding the event log.

nodes.title: GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/graph/projects/{id}
nodes.description: Reads one hosted project's snapshot, updates its project-level fields (journaling the change), or archives it — always scoped to the caller's owners.

nodes.title: GET /api/graph/projects/{id}/nodes
nodes.description: Read-only listing of a hosted project's nodes out of the stored snapshot, behind the shared graph:read guard chain.

nodes.title: GET /api/graph/projects/{id}/edges
nodes.description: Read-only listing of a hosted project's edges out of the stored snapshot, behind the shared graph:read guard chain.

nodes.title: GET /api/graph/projects/{id}/journal
nodes.description: Returns a hosted project's append-only journal in server seq order from the graph_events table.

nodes.title: GET /api/graph/projects/{id}/export
nodes.description: Assembles and returns the full ProjectBundle — snapshot plus journal — for download or migration back to local-first storage.

nodes.title: POST /api/graph/projects/{id}/mutations
nodes.description: The single write path for hosted graphs: applies validated mutation ops to the snapshot, bumps the concurrency version, and appends the emitted journal events atomically.

nodes.title: GET/POST/DELETE /api/graph/projects/{id}/repos
nodes.description: Manages a hosted project's repository links — repo, optional platform, optional monorepo path prefix — after checking the project belongs to the caller.

nodes.title: POST /api/publik
nodes.description: Publishes an anonymous, immutable snapshot: strips the journal, validates the bundle, stores it under a fresh id, and returns a one-time owner key — rate-limited per hashed IP.

nodes.title: GET/DELETE /api/publik/{id}
nodes.description: Serves a shared snapshot's bundle to anyone with the link, and deletes it for a caller presenting the matching owner key (verified against its stored hash).

nodes.title: POST /api/publik/{id}/report
nodes.description: Flags a shared snapshot by incrementing its report count, rate-limited per hashed IP like snapshot creation.

nodes.title: GET /api/synk/projects
nodes.description: Lists the signed-in user's backed-up projects with their latest backup info, read from the user-scoped Synk tables.

nodes.title: PUT/DELETE /api/synk/projects/{id}
nodes.description: Uploads a backup version of a local project — validated, sha256-deduped, journal included, tier limits enforced — or deletes the project and cascades away all its backups.

nodes.title: GET /api/synk/projects/{id}/backups
nodes.description: Lists the retained backup versions of one of the user's projects, newest first, without re-parsing the stored bundles.

nodes.title: GET /api/synk/backups/{id}
nodes.description: Downloads one backup's full bundle (journal intact) for restore, scoped to the session user's own rows.

nodes.title: GET /api/synk/ping
nodes.description: Minimal session-guarded probe — 401 without a session, otherwise ok plus the user — the template every authenticated service handler copies.

nodes.title: GET/POST /api/tokens
nodes.description: Session-only token management: lists an owner's API tokens and mints new scoped ones, returning the plaintext secret exactly once — a bearer token can never mint another token.

nodes.title: DELETE /api/tokens/{id}
nodes.description: Revokes an API token by stamping revoked_at, after verifying the session user belongs to the token's owner.

nodes.title: Create Project Dialog
nodes.description: Modal form capturing a title and optional description for a new empty project, destined for whichever section opened it.

nodes.title: Maps Index
nodes.description: Card grid of every reading the project offers — the built-in Journey and System maps plus custom maps stored in project metadata, each counted through its own renderer, with edit/delete on custom cards and a New map action.

nodes.title: Journey Map Canvas
nodes.description: The navigation-centered React Flow canvas: compose/playlist drill-down from the root with collapsible flows, visual duplication of reused views, full inline editing, a status/species minimap, and product-scoped empty states; the old /canvas URL redirects here.

nodes.title: System Map Canvas
nodes.description: The model-centered canvas joining views, API endpoints, and data models by cross-layer edges, with an organic/tiered layout switch, a hover-and-pin neighborhood spotlight that dims everything outside one node's relations, and the same minimap.

nodes.title: Map Editor Dialog
nodes.description: Dialog for authoring a custom map definition — id, title, kind, species and edge filters, root anchor picked from the project's nodes, product scope, depth, and layout hints.

nodes.title: Map Display Popover
nodes.description: Per-map Display button: toggle screenshot images on view cards, flow platform delivery as rings or bars, view platform availability as chips or rows, and whether minimap fills encode status or species — saved for this map alone.

nodes.title: Command Palette
nodes.description: The Cmd+K overlay: type-ahead over pages, maps, library sections, and in-place actions, with ranked matching, keyword synonyms, Tab completion, and Enter to navigate or run.

nodes.title: Keyboard Shortcuts Dialog
nodes.description: The Cmd+? reference dialog listing every chord the app answers to, grouped by scope, with the Mod key rendered as the running platform's own label.

nodes.title: Browse Maps
nodes.description: Open the maps index, pick a reading, and land on its renderer — Journey for the navigation drill-down, System for the model-centered picture, custom maps through whichever kind they declare.

nodes.title: Create Custom Map
nodes.description: Save a new reading of the graph from the maps index: open the editor dialog, name the map, choose kind, filters, anchor and scope, and the definition lands in project metadata as data an agent could equally have written.

nodes.title: Adjust Map Display
nodes.description: Tune how one map's cards read — images on or off, rings or bars, chips or rows, minimap color by status or species — from the Display popover on the open renderer, without touching any other map.

nodes.title: Edit Graph On Canvas
nodes.description: Grow the graph where it is drawn: add nodes, insert views between playlist steps, connect-to-create edges with a type prompt, and delete nodes or edges with confirmation, on either map canvas.

nodes.title: Navigate By Keyboard
nodes.description: Reach anything without the mouse: Cmd+K opens the palette to jump to a page, map, or action, and Cmd+? opens the shortcuts dialog to learn every chord the app answers to.

cases.label: Jump somewhere or run a command

nodes.title: Node Detail Panel
nodes.description: A column in the push-panel stack showing one node's editable fields (title, description, status, blocked-by, product), refs, platform variants with screenshots, species-specific editors, connections, invocation, and journal history.

nodes.title: Raw Bundle Panel
nodes.description: A panel-stack column that views the whole project bundle as JSON or YAML and, in guarded edit mode, saves changes back through the validated import path — which for the public sandbox replaces its in-memory state in place.

nodes.title: Library
nodes.description: The all-nodes inventory with gallery and directory display modes, species/search/blocked filters, product-scoped visibility, and a selection bar for bulk-moving nodes between products.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.description: The deliberately read-only 'where does this product stand?' dashboard composing platform gauges, parity, pyramid, delivery snapshot, release pulse, backlog, inventory, health, and maps cards.

nodes.title: Value Pyramid
nodes.description: The value-delivery radar: each value element carries status rings per platform, with a three-step filter and a switch between icon-led cards and one-line rows.

nodes.title: Acceptances Matrix
nodes.description: The coverage matrix grouping acceptances by their covered anchors, with per-platform status columns, parity-gap highlighting, value badges, and a filter bar over status, value, anchor, and search.

nodes.title: Edit Node Details
nodes.description: Open any node in the panel stack, autosave title, description, status, blocked-by and product membership inline, and drill into connected nodes by stacking further panels.

nodes.title: Edit Flow Playlist
nodes.description: Arrange a flow's ordered playlist in its detail panel — add views, sub-flows, conditions and junctions, create missing steps inline, and get cycle-blocked before a circular reference lands.

nodes.title: Edit Acceptance
nodes.description: Refine an acceptance in its detail panel: write the Gherkin scenario, pick the value elements it serves, set per-platform statuses, attach or detach cover anchors, and split it in two.

nodes.title: Browse Library
nodes.description: Sweep the whole node inventory — filter by species, search, or blocked state, create new nodes, bulk-move a selection between products, and open any node for detail editing.

nodes.title: Audit Value Coverage
nodes.description: Read the Overview, drill into the Value Pyramid, click an element through to its filtered acceptances in the matrix, and refine the ones that fall short.

nodes.title: Edit Raw Bundle
nodes.description: Open the project's raw bundle as JSON or YAML, edit it directly under an unsaved-changes guard, and save back only what the bundle validator accepts.

nodes.title: Changelog
nodes.description: Two-panel project changelog: a Design funnel (backlog, commitments, decision activity) beside a Delivery panel of unreleased deliverables and release cards grouped by tagged version.

nodes.title: History
nodes.description: Granular newest-first feed of every journal event, filterable by family chips (nodes, edges, decisions, delivery, ideas & requests, references).

nodes.title: Decision Log
nodes.description: ADR-style list of the project's decision nodes ordered by decided date, filterable by decision status, with a dialog to log a new decision.

nodes.title: Decision Editor
nodes.description: Detail panel for one decision: autosaving context, consequences, and decided-at fields plus a decision-status select that keeps the lifecycle status in sync.

nodes.title: Delivery Board
nodes.description: Kanban of nodes as per-platform delivery items in lifecycle-status columns, with platform, species, status-preset, and search filters and node creation.

nodes.title: Review Changelog
nodes.description: Scan what the project has shipped and committed to — releases, deliverables, backlog, and decision activity — and jump into a decision straight from the feed.

entries.label: Open a decision from the feed?

nodes.title: Audit Project History
nodes.description: Trace exactly what happened and when by browsing the full journal event feed and narrowing it to one event family.

nodes.title: Log a Decision
nodes.description: Record a product decision from the Decision Log — name the What, then fill in context, consequences, status, and decided date in its editor.

nodes.title: Track Delivery Status
nodes.description: Follow work across the lifecycle on the delivery board, filtering by platform, species, or search to find and update the items that matter.

nodes.title: Public Snapshot Page
nodes.description: The /p/{id} preview page for a shared Publik snapshot — title, node/edge counts, format-level badge, no-retention disclaimer, and an Import into arkaik action.

nodes.title: Publish Dialog
nodes.description: Two-stage confirm/result dialog that publishes a project to Publik and shows the share URL and one-time owner key, surfacing validation findings, rate limits, and size errors.

nodes.title: Synk Onboarding Banner
nodes.description: Dismissible banner on the projects page offering one-click Synk backup for each browser-held project after sign-in — the Lokal-to-Synk conversion funnel.

nodes.title: Synk Restore Dialog
nodes.description: Dialog that lists the account's Synk projects and their backups, and restores a chosen backup's bundle into this browser.

nodes.title: Account Menu
nodes.description: Sign-in button / account dropdown in the app chrome — GitHub sign-in, profile, a link to agent tokens, and sign-out; renders nothing when auth is unconfigured.

nodes.title: Agent Tokens Settings
nodes.description: The /settings/tokens page where the user creates (shown once, stored hashed) and revokes tokens that let the arkaik CLI and MCP server act as them.

nodes.title: Generate With AI
nodes.description: The /generate prompt builder — pick a mode (from pitch, from plan, extend map), configure the project, and copy an assembled LLM prompt that yields an importable bundle.

nodes.title: Publish to Publik
nodes.description: Share a project anonymously: confirm what becomes public, publish the bundle (journal stripped server-side), save the one-time owner key, and open the unlisted snapshot page.

nodes.title: Sign In with GitHub
nodes.description: Authenticate via the GitHub OAuth dance from the account menu; signing in changes nothing but this button — no local feature is account-gated.

nodes.title: Back Up with Synk
nodes.description: Keep browser-held projects backed up to the account: accept the onboarding offer (or use per-project Back up now), then restore a backup into any browser later.

nodes.title: Move Project to Account
nodes.description: Promote a browser-held project to a hosted one from its card (shown only when signed in): the bundle is copied to the server under a new prj_ id, the local original stays, and the agent plane opens up.

nodes.title: Generate Map with AI
nodes.description: Acceptance-first intake for a new map: build a tailored LLM prompt from an idea or plan, run it elsewhere, then hand off to import with the intended destination preserved.

nodes.title: Export Project Bundle
nodes.description: Get the whole project out as a portable JSON bundle — download it from the project menu (with a size warning past 4 MB), or inspect and copy it in the raw bundle panel.

entries.label: How do you want the bundle?

nodes.title: Explore Public Sandbox
nodes.description: Open Arkaik's own map from the Explore section — signed in or out — and play with everything for real in per-tab memory: refresh resets to the pristine seed, or keep what you built by importing a copy.

cases.label: Import a copy as a real local project

nodes.title: Sandbox Notice
nodes.description: The amber sidebar notice on the public self-map telling visitors changes stay in this tab and vanish on refresh; the Reset and Import-a-copy actions live in the project switcher menu.

nodes.title: Browse Documentation
nodes.description: Read Arkaik's in-app docs site, reached from the project menu, with sidebar navigation and full-text search across pages.

nodes.title: Documentation Site
nodes.description: The /docs pages — server-rendered markdown with a collapsible sidebar tree and a search box over the cached page index.

nodes.title: CLI Terminal
nodes.description: The terminal surface of the arkaik CLI — usage text, command output, validation findings, and journal listings rendered to stdout.

nodes.title: Arkaik Agent Skill
nodes.description: The generated SKILL.md doctrine an agent reads — installed by arkaik init or the Claude Code plugin, with its schema reference and standalone validator alongside.

nodes.title: MCP Tool Catalog
nodes.description: The arkaik-mcp server's agent-facing surface — fourteen read and write tools whose JSON results are the same projections humans see as pages.

nodes.title: Initialize Repo Map
nodes.description: arkaik init scaffolds docs/arkaik/ (bundle, journal, assets), writes the union-merge rule, and installs the templated agent skill into the repo (--update upgrades).

nodes.title: Validate Bundle
nodes.description: arkaik validate (and the zero-dependency validate-bundle.js artifact) runs @arkaik/schema shape, semantic, and snapshot-journal cross-checks as the toolchain's hard gate.

nodes.title: Journal & Release
nodes.description: arkaik log prints the project changelog or a node timeline, arkaik release tags a version and drafts its notes, and arkaik deliverable records a shipped deliverable.

nodes.title: Sync External Refs
nodes.description: arkaik sync mirrors GitHub issue and PR status into node refs, updating external_status/synced_at and appending ref.status_changed events.

nodes.title: Pack, Open & Push
nodes.description: arkaik pack produces a single self-contained interchange bundle, arkaik open validates and hands it to arkaik.app import, and arkaik push publishes it to Publik (or deletes a snapshot with its owner key).

nodes.title: Link Hosted Project
nodes.description: arkaik link points the repo at a hosted account project by writing docs/arkaik/arkaik.json, listing and verifying the projects an ARKAIK_TOKEN can reach.

nodes.title: MCP Agent Session
nodes.description: An agent host spawns arkaik-mcp over stdio and reads or mutates the map through validator-gated dual-write tools, against the repo bundle or a linked hosted project.

nodes.title: Project Settings
nodes.description: The project's settings page: linked repositories for PR-driven transitions, the product manager, and the delete danger zone.

nodes.title: Landing Page
nodes.description: The signed-out front door — living logo, ASCII terrain, and a Start building call to action; signed-in visitors are redirected straight to the projects home.

nodes.title: Manage Products
nodes.description: Declare, rename, and remove the project's products and their platform menus from the Settings page.

nodes.title: Sections mirror where projects live
nodes.description: Signed in, the projects page groups every project under Hosted, Synked, or Lokal according to where it actually lives — a browser project counts as Synked only when Synk really holds a backup for it.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user with an account-hosted project, a browser project backed up to Synk, and a browser-only project
When the projects page loads
Then the three projects appear under the Hosted, Synked, and Lokal sections respectively, each heading showing its count

nodes.title: Deletion cannot happen by accident
nodes.description: A project can only be deleted from its Settings page's Danger zone, behind a confirmation dialog — the listing card carries no delete button at all.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a user on the Settings page of a project they own
When they click "Delete project" in the Danger zone
Then a confirmation dialog names the project and asks first, and only confirming archives it and returns them to the projects listing

nodes.title: Public map cannot be deleted
nodes.description: The built-in public self-map offers no delete control anywhere — its Settings page renders no Danger zone, so the shared fixture cannot be removed even deliberately.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the Settings page of the built-in public self-map project
When the user looks for a way to delete it
Then no Danger zone, delete button, or confirmation dialog is offered

nodes.title: Examples are one click away
nodes.description: An empty Lokal shelf — including the signed-out empty state — offers the example project picker, and choosing one imports the bundle into this browser and opens it immediately.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a visitor with no Lokal projects on the projects page
When they pick "Pebbles" or "Arkaik" from the "Import example project" select
Then the example bundle is imported into this browser as a Lokal project and the app navigates straight into it

nodes.title: Signed in skips the pitch
nodes.description: A signed-in visitor to the landing page is redirected straight to their projects instead of being asked to press "Start building" again.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a visitor with a valid session
When they open the landing page at "/"
Then they are redirected to /projects without seeing the pitch or pressing "Start building"

nodes.title: Create lands where you asked
nodes.description: Creating a project from a section's menu makes the new project in that section's home — account, Synk-backed browser, or this browser only — and opens it right away.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the create dialog opened from the Synked section's create menu
When the user enters a title and submits
Then an empty project is created in this browser with a Synk backup, appears under Synked, and the app navigates into it

nodes.title: Signing in adds, never rearranges
nodes.description: Projects held in this browser stay exactly where they are when the user signs in — Hosted and Synked sections appear alongside Lokal rather than absorbing or moving anything.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-out visitor with projects stored in this browser
When they sign in and return to the projects page
Then every browser project is still listed under Lokal, untouched, with Hosted and Synked sections added around it

nodes.title: Move to account keeps the original
nodes.description: Moving a browser-held project to the account is a copy, not a transfer — the hosted twin gets its own id and the local original stays put, so a failure loses nothing.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user viewing a browser-held project's card
When they click "Move to account"
Then a copy with a new server-owned id appears under Hosted and the original project remains in this browser

nodes.title: Products are named in Settings
nodes.description: The Settings page's Products panel lets a project name the family of apps sharing its graph, so every other page can scope to one product.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project's Settings page
When the user adds a product in the Products panel
Then the product joins the project's product list with its member count, and product-scoped pages can select it

nodes.title: Map cards count honestly
nodes.description: A map card on the index never advertises a node or edge count the map it links to does not show, because each map is counted through the renderer that draws it.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project with a stored journey map anchored below the project root
When the maps index renders its cards
Then each card's node and edge counts come from the same selection the map's own renderer draws, and opening the map shows at least the counted nodes

nodes.title: Drill down without leaving
nodes.description: Expanding a flow on the Journey map unfolds its playlist inline on the same canvas, and collapsing it restores the overview without a page change.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the Journey map with a top-level flow collapsed
When the user clicks to expand that flow
Then its playlist unfolds in place on the same canvas, any other expanded top-level journey collapses, and collapsing it again returns to the overview with no navigation

nodes.title: Scoped journey never lies
nodes.description: A journey whose anchor does not resolve inside the named product renders an empty state that names the reason and offers the System map, never another product's graph.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a product scope is active and the journey's anchor is missing or not part of that product
When the Journey map renders
Then the canvas is replaced by an empty state saying which of the two went wrong, with a link to the System map, and no other product's nodes are drawn

nodes.title: Display choices stick per map
nodes.description: A display option flipped in the popover is saved against that map's id alone, survives a reload, and leaves every other map's rendering untouched.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the Journey map showing screenshot images on view cards
When the user hides images from the Display popover and reloads the page
Then the Journey still hides images while the System map and every custom map keep their own display, because the choice was stored under this map's id only

nodes.title: No circular playlists
nodes.description: Inserting a flow into a playlist that would make it contain itself, directly or indirectly, is refused with a circular-reference message and leaves the graph unchanged.

metadata.gherkin:
Given flow A already appears in flow B's playlist chain
When the user tries to add B into A's playlist from the canvas
Then the insertion is refused with a message naming the circular reference, and a node created for the attempt is rolled back so the graph stays valid

nodes.title: Only valid connections offered
nodes.description: Dragging a connection between two cards opens a dialog that offers only the relationship types that ordered species pair admits.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the user drags a connection from a view card onto a data-model card on either canvas
When the edge-type dialog opens
Then it lists only the edge types valid for that source and target species, so an invalid relationship cannot be created by hand

nodes.title: Deletion always asks first
nodes.description: Deleting a node from the canvas or with the Delete key opens a confirmation that names the node, counts its descendants, and makes cascade an explicit opt-in.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a flow with descendant nodes and its panel open on the Journey map
When the user presses Delete or chooses to delete it
Then a confirmation dialog names the node, offers "Also delete N child node(s)" as an unchecked option, and nothing is removed until the user confirms

nodes.title: Insert between playlist steps
nodes.description: A view, flow, condition, or junction can be inserted between two playlist steps right on the canvas, landing at that exact position with its compose edge created when missing.

metadata.gherkin:
Given an expanded flow on the Journey map
When the user inserts a view between two of its playlist steps
Then the entry is placed at exactly that position in the playlist and a composes edge from the flow is added if one did not already exist

nodes.title: Custom maps are saved data
nodes.description: Saving the New map dialog writes a map definition into project metadata — reserved built-in ids and duplicates refused by name — and the map appears in the index, the sidebar, and the command palette.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the New map dialog filled with a title, a kind, and an anchor picked by search
When the user saves
Then the definition lands in project metadata as data an agent could equally write, ids shadowing "journey" or "system" or an existing map are refused with a named error, and the new map shows up on the maps index and in the command palette

nodes.title: Jump anywhere from keyboard
nodes.description: The command palette ranks every project destination as you type, matches the synonyms people actually use, completes with Tab, and navigates or runs on Enter.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the command palette opened with the mod key and K
When the user types "screens"
Then the Views destination ranks first through its synonym, Tab fills the input with the active row's wording, and Enter lands on the library filtered to views

nodes.title: Shortcut list tells no lies
nodes.description: The shortcuts dialog lists every chord the current surface actually answers to — project and map chords are hidden outside a project — and renders the mod key as the running platform's own label.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the shortcuts dialog opened from the docs shell, outside any project
When its groups render
Then only chords live everywhere are listed, project-only and map-only chords are absent, and the Mod token shows as the platform's own key label

nodes.title: Canvas stays where left
nodes.description: The viewport never jumps while you work: editing data re-lays the graph without moving your framing, and the canvas re-frames only on changes you asked for, like a layout switch or a panel opening.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the System map panned and zoomed onto one corner of the graph
When the user edits a node so the layout recomputes
Then the viewport keeps its position, and it re-frames only after an asked-for change such as switching the layout rendition or opening or closing a panel

nodes.title: Spotlight one node's relations
nodes.description: On the dense System map, hovering a node — or having one selected in a panel — dims everything outside its direct relations so one node's neighborhood stays readable in the whole-product picture.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the System map showing the whole product
When the user hovers a data-model card, or a node is pinned by its open panel
Then every node and edge outside that node's direct relations dims, and moving the pointer away restores the full picture

nodes.title: Two readings of the system
nodes.description: The System map re-draws the same nodes as either an organic cluster layout or tiered species rows — views over endpoints over data models — and re-frames the viewport on each switch.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the System map open in its default organic rendition
When the user switches the layout select to Tiered
Then the same nodes re-lay out into species tiers with views above API endpoints above data models, the viewport re-frames to the new layout, and switching back restores the organic clustering

nodes.title: Detail edits autosave
nodes.description: Title, description, and blocked-by edits in the detail panel persist on a short debounce — there is no save button to forget.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the detail panel is open on a node
When the user edits the title or description and pauses typing for 350ms
Then the change is persisted without pressing any save button and survives closing and reopening the panel

nodes.title: Playlists cannot loop
nodes.description: Adding a sub-flow that would make a flow contain itself, directly or through intermediates, is refused with an explanation instead of corrupting the graph.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a flow's playlist editor is open
When the user adds a sub-flow entry that would make the flow contain itself, directly or via intermediate flows
Then the entry is not added and an error toast names the flow that would create the circular reference

nodes.title: Playlists branch inline
nodes.description: A flow's playlist mixes views, sub-flows, binary conditions, and multi-way junctions, edited in place from the detail panel.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a flow's playlist editor is open
When the user adds a condition entry with a question label and fills its true and false branches
Then the branch structure persists in the flow's playlist and each referenced view or sub-flow resolves to a real node

nodes.title: Raw edits gated by validation
nodes.description: Saving from the raw bundle panel parses the draft and runs it through the same validated import path — malformed JSON or YAML never reaches storage.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the raw bundle panel is in edit mode with a draft containing invalid syntax or a schema violation
When the user confirms save
Then the save is rejected with a specific error message and the stored bundle is unchanged

nodes.title: Format switch preserves draft
nodes.description: Switching the raw panel between JSON and YAML re-serializes the current draft; a draft that cannot parse blocks the switch instead of mangling the text.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the raw bundle panel is in edit mode with unsaved edits
When the user switches between JSON and YAML
Then a parseable draft is carried over re-serialized in the new format, and an unparseable draft blocks the switch with an error toast leaving the text intact

nodes.title: Unsaved raw edits guarded
nodes.description: Closing or cancelling the raw bundle panel with unsaved edits asks for confirmation before anything is discarded.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the raw bundle panel is in edit mode with unsaved changes
When the user cancels or closes the panel
Then a confirmation dialog intercepts the action and the draft is only discarded after the user confirms

nodes.title: Gherkin and values inline
nodes.description: An acceptance's Given/When/Then scenario and its value elements are edited in place in the acceptance editor, debounce-saved like every other detail field.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the acceptance editor is open on an acceptance node
When the user edits the gherkin text and toggles value elements in the value picker
Then both persist without a save button and a concurrent status edit is not overwritten by the debounced gherkin save

nodes.title: Split keeps the context
nodes.description: Splitting one acceptance into several pieces carries the covers edges, platforms, and product to every piece — and says so on screen before you commit.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the split dialog is open on an acceptance covering n nodes
When the user names at least two pieces and confirms the split
Then each new acceptance covers the same n nodes with the same platforms and product, and the dialog stated that carry-over before submission

nodes.title: Parity gaps surface themselves
nodes.description: An acceptance carries per-platform statuses, and the matrix's parity-gap toggle narrows to exactly the acceptances whose platforms disagree.

metadata.gherkin:
Given an acceptance whose platforms resolve to different statuses
When the user enables the parity-gap filter on the acceptances matrix
Then that acceptance remains listed while acceptances with uniform platform statuses are filtered out, and each anchor group shows its gap count

nodes.title: Matrix groups by anchor
nodes.description: The acceptances matrix groups every promise under the view or flow it covers, with unanchored intake ideas kept last and reachable by a dedicated filter.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project with acceptances covering views and flows plus some covering nothing
When the user opens the acceptances matrix
Then acceptances appear under each anchor they cover (once per anchor), anchor groups sort by title, and the Unanchored bucket is last and selectable via the anchor filter

nodes.title: Value coverage at a glance
nodes.description: The pyramid lays out the 30 value elements by tier, each showing how many acceptances serve it and their status rollup.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project whose acceptances carry value elements
When the user opens the pyramid page
Then every value element appears in its tier with its acceptance count and a status rollup labelled in acceptances, and served elements are visually distinct from unserved ones

nodes.title: Unserved values filterable
nodes.description: The pyramid toolbar steps between empty, all, and addressed elements, so the value elements no acceptance serves are one click away.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the pyramid page is open
When the user steps the toolbar filter to 'empty'
Then only value elements with zero covering acceptances remain visible, exposing where the product currently makes no promise

nodes.title: Bulk selection stays honest
nodes.description: Library selection survives filter changes, the action bar counts by species, and it warns how many selected nodes the current filter is hiding before a bulk product move.

metadata.gherkin:
Given several nodes are selected in the library and the search filter then hides some of them
When the user reads the selection bar and moves the selection to a product
Then the bar states how many selected nodes are hidden by the filter and the move touches every selected node, not just the visible ones

nodes.title: Doc health always visible
nodes.description: The overview reports the map's blind spots — nodes unreachable from root, views without screenshots, missing descriptions, disconnected nodes, open backlog — as counted indicators.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project with an orphan flow, a view without a screenshot, and a node without a description
When the user opens the overview page
Then each health indicator reports the offending count against its denominator and lists the offending node ids deterministically

nodes.title: History Never Rewritten
nodes.description: The journal is append-only: recorded events are read as written forever, even legacy status ids from before a rename.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project journal containing a status event recorded with a pre-v3 status id
When I open the History page after later changes to the same node
Then the original event still reads exactly as it was written, with no rewritten or deleted lines

nodes.title: Filter History by Family
nodes.description: The full event feed narrows to one event family — nodes, edges, decisions, delivery, ideas and requests, or references — with a single chip.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a History page showing events of several types
When I click the Decisions family chip
Then only decision events remain in the feed, and clicking the chip again returns to all events

nodes.title: Design and Delivery Apart
nodes.description: The changelog separates the design funnel (backlog, commitments, decisions) from the delivery record (unreleased work, releases) into two side-by-side panels.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project with open backlog items, commitment transitions, and shipped deliverables
When I open the Changelog page
Then a Design panel shows backlog, commitments, and decisions, and a separate Delivery panel shows unreleased work and releases

nodes.title: Deliverables Anchor When Shipped
nodes.description: A deliverable belongs to the release whose slice contains its first occurrence; later edits update its content without ever moving it between releases.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a deliverable first recorded between the 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 release tags
When the same deliverable id is re-appended later with an edited summary
Then the 1.3.0 release card shows the updated summary and the deliverable still belongs to 1.3.0

nodes.title: Unreleased Work Stays Visible
nodes.description: Deliverables shipped after the most recent release tag surface under an Unreleased heading instead of disappearing until the next version.

metadata.gherkin:
Given deliverables recorded after the most recent release tag
When I open the Changelog's Delivery panel
Then those deliverables appear under an Unreleased heading, above the releases, until a new version is tagged

nodes.title: Decisions Keep Their Why
nodes.description: A decision records its context (why), consequences (how), and the date it was decided, and keeps all three on every future read.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a decision node open in the detail panel
When I fill in Context, Consequences, and a Decided-on date and close the panel
Then reopening the decision later shows the same why, how, and date

nodes.title: Decision Edits Save Themselves
nodes.description: Context, consequences, and date edits autosave shortly after typing stops — there is no save button, and concurrent edits to different fields never clobber each other.

metadata.gherkin:
Given I am typing into a decision's Context field
When I pause typing without pressing any save button
Then the edit persists automatically, and an edit made to Consequences at the same time is not lost

nodes.title: Superseded Decisions Stay Traceable
nodes.description: A replaced decision is never deleted: it nests dimmed under the decision that superseded it, and its full record stays one click away.

metadata.gherkin:
Given decision B supersedes decision A
When I view the Decision Log
Then A appears nested and dimmed under B rather than removed, and opening A still shows its full record

nodes.title: Filter Decisions by Status
nodes.description: Status chips with live counts narrow the decision log to one decision state, shown as a flat list.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a Decision Log holding decisions in several decision states
When I click a status filter chip
Then only decisions in that state are listed, flat, and each chip's count matches the log

nodes.title: Board Mirrors the Lifecycle
nodes.description: The delivery board groups every node into the column of its current lifecycle status, narrowed by species, platform, and search filters.

metadata.gherkin:
Given nodes spread across the lifecycle from idea to live
When I open the Delivery board
Then each item sits in the column of its current status, and the species, platform, and search filters narrow the board

nodes.title: One Card per Platform
nodes.description: A node appears once per platform it targets, each card in that platform's own status column — uneven delivery is visible, not averaged away.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a view that is live on web but in development on iOS
When I view the Delivery board with all platforms shown
Then the view appears as two cards — one in the Live column for web and one in the Development column for iOS

nodes.title: Empty History Is Calm
nodes.description: A bundle without a journal renders a quiet empty state on the changelog and history pages — never an error.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project whose bundle carries no journal events
When I open the Changelog or History page
Then I see a gentle empty state explaining history will appear once recorded, not an error

nodes.title: Publishing never leaks history
nodes.description: A Publik snapshot never contains the project's journal: the strip is enforced server-side, not left to client behavior.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a local project whose bundle embeds a journal of change events
When the user publishes it from the publish dialog (which sends no include_journal opt-in)
Then the snapshot stored and served at /api/publik/{id} contains no journal[] — the server strips it unless a request explicitly asks ?include_journal=true

nodes.title: Owner key shown once
nodes.description: After publishing, the dialog shows the share URL and owner key exactly once, with copy buttons and a save-this-key warning — the server keeps only a hash.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a publish just succeeded
When the success stage of the publish dialog renders
Then the share URL and owner key appear with copy buttons and a warning that the key will not be shown again — the server stores only its SHA-256 hash and can never return it

nodes.title: Deletion gated by key
nodes.description: Only the holder of the owner key can delete a snapshot, and snapshots are immutable — so a leaked link can neither edit nor remove what you shared.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a published snapshot
When DELETE /api/publik/{id} arrives with a bearer key whose SHA-256 does not match the stored hash
Then the server answers 403 and the snapshot is untouched — and because snapshots have no update endpoint, nobody can edit one either; re-publishing mints a new id

nodes.title: Publish without an account
nodes.description: Sharing a graph requires no sign-up: publishing is anonymous and the snapshot lives at an unguessable, unlisted URL.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a visitor with no arkaik account and no session
When they publish a project from the publish dialog
Then the snapshot is created with no sign-in step anywhere in the flow, at a server-generated URL-safe id of at least 64 bits of randomness, and there is no public listing that could reveal it

nodes.title: Anyone imports a copy
nodes.description: Anyone with a snapshot URL can import it as a fresh local project — the shared original and any existing local projects are never disturbed.

metadata.gherkin:
Given anyone opens /p/{id} for a shared snapshot
When they click "Import into arkaik"
Then the bundle is fetched client-side and imported through the same funnel as a manual JSON import, with ID-collision rewriting, so it lands as a new local project and overwrites nothing

nodes.title: Backups run themselves
nodes.description: Once a project is backed up to Synk, every later edit is backed up automatically about a minute after you stop typing — no button to remember.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user editing a local project that Synk backs up
When roughly 60 seconds pass after their last mutation
Then the sync engine exports, canonically serializes, and PUTs the bundle to /api/synk/projects/{id} with no user action, and the project's visible status becomes "backed up"

nodes.title: Backups dedupe by content
nodes.description: A backup whose canonical bytes match the latest stored version records nothing, so the version list only ever contains real changes.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project whose latest Synk backup has SHA-256 hash H
When a backup attempt PUTs a bundle whose canonical serialization also hashes to H
Then the server answers 200 with { deduped: true } and stores no new version, so the restore dialog's version list holds only genuinely different states

nodes.title: Failed backups lose nothing
nodes.description: A network failure or tier-limit refusal never touches the local data: the bundle stays in the browser and the next edit or a manual retry backs it up.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a backup attempt that fails with a network error or a 403 limit response
When the failure lands
Then the local bundle in IndexedDB is untouched, the project status shows the error (with structured limit/actual/tier details on a 403), and the next mutation or an explicit "Back up now" retries — the engine never writes server state into local storage

nodes.title: Restore never overwrites
nodes.description: Restoring a retained version always creates a new local project — it can never clobber the live project you restored from.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user who picked a retained version in the restore dialog
When they click Restore
Then the backup's bundle is imported through the standard import funnel with ID-collision rewriting, landing as a NEW local project the app navigates to — the existing local project is never overwritten in place

nodes.title: One-click backup offer
nodes.description: After signing in, each local project without a backup is offered for backup with a single click — the data never moves, it only gains a copy.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user whose projects page lists local projects with no Synk backup
When the page renders
Then a dismissible banner offers one "Back up" button per candidate — excluding hosted projects, the seed sandbox, and already-backed-up ones — and the banner disappears on its own once no candidates remain and never shows to signed-out users

nodes.title: Moving keeps local copy
nodes.description: "Move to account" is a copy: the hosted project gets a new server-owned id and the browser-held original stays exactly where it was.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a browser-held project and a signed-in user who clicks "Move to account"
When the hosted copy is created
Then it receives a new server-owned id (prj_…) while the local original remains untouched in the browser — and if the move fails midway, nothing has been lost or deleted

nodes.title: Token secret shown once
nodes.description: An agent token's plaintext appears exactly once at mint, scoped to what you chose, and a leaked token can never mint another or widen its own scopes.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a signed-in user on /settings/tokens who names a token and picks its scopes
When the mint succeeds
Then the plaintext secret is shown once in a dismissable panel that says it cannot be recovered, the server stores only a hash, and the token stays revocable from the list — token management itself is session-only, so the token cannot manage tokens

nodes.title: Sign-in never gates local
nodes.description: Every local-first surface works with no account and even with no auth configured — services degrade to absent instead of breaking the app.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a deployment with no auth environment variables set
When the app boots
Then every local-first surface works normally while the sign-in button, account menu, and token settings render nothing at all — and on a configured deployment, staying signed out still gates no local feature

nodes.title: One prompt, any LLM
nodes.description: The generate page assembles a complete, copyable prompt for whatever LLM you already use — arkaik calls no AI and needs no API key — then hands you back to import the result.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a user on /generate who chose a use case, platforms, and target LLM
When they click Copy or Download
Then a complete prompt with a token estimate lands on the clipboard or as a .txt file to paste into any LLM, and the "I've got my JSON — import it" handoff returns them to /projects with the right import target preselected

nodes.title: Old Bundles Still Import
nodes.description: A bundle exported under an older status vocabulary imports through the lenient parse + migrate path instead of being refused.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a bundle exported under a pre-v3 status vocabulary
When the user imports the JSON file
Then the shape parse accepts the legacy statuses, migrates them to the current vocabulary before validation, and the project opens with every node intact

nodes.title: Broken Imports Explain Themselves
nodes.description: An invalid bundle is refused with a readable, path-specific message rather than a silent failure or a corrupted project.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a JSON file whose bundle has a duplicate node id and a dangling edge reference
When the user imports it
Then the import is refused with a message naming each failing path and its problem, capped at five findings so the error stays readable

nodes.title: Reserved IDs Stay Reserved
nodes.description: An imported bundle can never squat the public seed id or the hosted prj_ namespace, so id-based routing stays a total function.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a bundle whose project id is "arkaik-self-map" or starts with "prj_"
When the user imports it
Then a fresh unique id is minted and rewritten across the project, its nodes, and its edges, and the reserved namespaces remain untouched

nodes.title: Your Map Leaves With You
nodes.description: One click downloads the complete project — nodes, edges, and journal — as a portable JSON bundle, so the data is never locked in.

metadata.gherkin:
Given an open project
When the user exports it
Then a JSON file named "<title>-<id>.json" downloads containing the project metadata, all nodes, all edges, and the app-emitted journal

nodes.title: Exports Re-import Cleanly
nodes.description: An exported bundle round-trips: importing the file back yields a working copy with no manual fix-up.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a project exported to a JSON file
When that same file is imported back
Then a working copy opens with identical nodes and edges, under a freshly minted id when the original id is already taken

nodes.title: Refresh Restores Pristine Seed
nodes.description: Nothing done in the public self-map sandbox persists — a page refresh restores the pristine seed, so it cannot be broken.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a visitor has created, edited, and deleted nodes in the public self-map sandbox
When they refresh the page
Then the pristine seed is restored and none of their changes were persisted to IndexedDB or the network

nodes.title: Sandbox Edits Are Real
nodes.description: The public self-map is the full product, not a demo reel: every editor works and writes append journal events in memory like any project.

metadata.gherkin:
Given an anonymous visitor opens /project/arkaik-self-map
When they create a node and rewire an edge
Then the changes apply immediately in the tab with journal events appended, exactly as on a real project

nodes.title: Sandbox Rules Stated Plainly
nodes.description: A persistent sidebar notice tells the visitor their changes are tab-local and vanish on refresh, before any surprise can happen.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the public self-map is open
When the project sidebar renders
Then a notice states that changes stay in this tab and vanish on refresh

nodes.title: Docs Live In App
nodes.description: The repo's documentation renders inside the product at /docs, with the README as Overview and every page reachable by navigation or search.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a visitor opens /docs
When the page loads
Then the repo README renders as the Overview and every documentation page is reachable from the sidebar navigation and the search palette

nodes.title: One Command Repo Setup
nodes.description: A single `npx arkaik init` gives any repo a valid bundle, a journal wired for union merge, and the installed agent skill.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a repository with no Arkaik artifacts
When the user runs `npx arkaik init`
Then docs/arkaik/bundle.json (a valid empty bundle), journal.jsonl, the assets dir, the .gitattributes union-merge rule, and .claude/skills/arkaik/SKILL.md all exist after the one command

nodes.title: Re-run Init Safely
nodes.description: Re-running init never overwrites an existing bundle, journal, or locally edited skill; only `--update` upgrades the skill, gated on its version stamp, and even then never touches the bundle or journal.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a repo where `arkaik init` already ran and the bundle has local edits
When the user runs `arkaik init` again
Then every existing artifact is reported as skipped and no file content changes, and a subsequent `arkaik init --update` with the same packaged skill version is a no-op

nodes.title: One Skill Doctrine Everywhere
nodes.description: The agent skill installed by `arkaik init` and the one shipped in the Claude Code plugin are renders of the same source, with schema reference and validator generated from @arkaik/schema and drift-checked in CI.

metadata.gherkin:
Given the skill assets generated from @arkaik/schema
When a schema change lands without regenerating the CLI's packaged skill assets and the plugin's copies
Then the CI drift check fails the build, so `arkaik init` installs and the plugin ships cannot teach different doctrines

nodes.title: Validator Blocks Broken Bundles
nodes.description: `arkaik validate` exits non-zero with pathed findings on any shape or semantic error — duplicate ids, dangling edges, playlist cycles — so a broken bundle is caught before it is committed; warnings never fail the run.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a bundle where an edge's target_id references a node that does not exist
When the user runs `arkaik validate docs/arkaik/bundle.json`
Then the command prints an ERROR finding with the rule and path, reports INVALID, and exits 1 without modifying any file

nodes.title: Bad Line Damages Nothing
nodes.description: A malformed journal line invalidates exactly one event — the validator reports it by line number — and can never damage existing history or the snapshot, because one JSONL line is one self-contained event.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a journal.jsonl containing one truncated JSON line among valid events
When the user runs `arkaik validate` on the sibling bundle
Then the report names the malformed line by number as a single finding, every other event still parses, and the bundle snapshot is untouched

nodes.title: Parallel Appends Merge Cleanly
nodes.description: Because init writes the journal's merge=union rule and every event is one self-contained line, two branches that each appended events merge in git without conflict, and consumers reorder by timestamp and id.

metadata.gherkin:
Given two git branches that each appended different events to journal.jsonl
When the branches are merged
Then git's union merge combines both sets of lines with no conflict markers and `arkaik validate` still reports the journal as parseable

nodes.title: Release Notes Draft Themselves
nodes.description: `arkaik release <version>` appends exactly one validated release.tagged marker to the journal and prints a release-note draft of everything since the previous release — the bundle file is never rewritten, so validate stays green.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a journal with events accumulated since the last release marker
When the user runs `arkaik release 1.2.0`
Then journal.jsonl grows by exactly one release.tagged line, a draft listing the since-last-release deliverables and events is printed, and the bundle file's bytes are unchanged

nodes.title: Linked Repo Fails Loud
nodes.description: A repo linked to a hosted project but missing its token exits non-zero instead of silently falling back to the local bundle — an agent is never served a stale graph that looks fine.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a repo with docs/arkaik/arkaik.json linking a hosted project and no ARKAIK_TOKEN in the environment
When an agent session starts arkaik-mcp
Then the server exits non-zero with an explicit token error and never answers tool calls from the repo's local bundle

nodes.title: Sync Mirrors, Never Overrides
nodes.description: `arkaik sync` mirrors each external ref's live status into external_status/synced_at and appends one ref.status_changed event per change, while node.status is never touched and unchanged or unknown refs are left alone.

metadata.gherkin:
Given a node whose GitHub PR ref is mirrored as "open" and the PR has since merged
When the user runs `arkaik sync` with a GitHub token in the environment

nodes.title: Share Validated, History Private
nodes.description: `arkaik push` publishes a shareable snapshot URL straight from the terminal, but only after the full validation gate passes — and the journal is stripped by default, so history never leaves the repo unless explicitly included.

nodes.title: Token Never Touches Disk
nodes.description: `arkaik link` writes only the project id and instance origin to a commit-safe file; the access token is read from the environment at run time and is never written anywhere git could remember it.

metadata.gherkin:

When the user runs `arkaik link --project prj_123`
Then docs/arkaik/arkaik.json contains only the project_id and remote origin, and the token string appears in no file the command wrote

nodes.title: Agents Write Validator-Gated
nodes.description: Every mutating MCP tool applies the change in memory, runs the full validator, and only on success persists journal events plus the canonical snapshot — a rejected mutation returns pathed findings and writes nothing.

When the agent calls add_edge with a source/target pair the schema's edge semantics forbid
Then the tool result is a refusal carrying the validator's pathed findings, and neither bundle.json nor journal.jsonl was modified — while a valid mutation appends its events and rewrites the snapshot canonically in the same call
